描述_ZN: Wisteria scroll, Qing dynasty, by Wu Changshuo, on gold paper and color, 163.4 cm in length and 47.3 cm in width.　　This picture was made by Wu Changshuo in 1905 at the age of 62, and is the last of a four-strip screen of flowers. Paragraph: "On the eighth day of the eighth month of the eighth year of the year Yisi (1905), Wu Junqing of Anji drew up the Thirteen Peaks Cao Tang. Inscription: "Seal of Wu Junzhi". The painted vine leaves are leaning in the air like a dragon flying and a phoenix dancing. The vines are coiled and twisted, wrapping around the stone several times. The author skillfully uses the brushwork like wild grass, and the painting is swift and complete in a single breath. At the same time, the painting draws air rather than form, pursuing the aesthetic interest of the calligraphic air that penetrates the mind. As he said, "Cursive calligraphy is for grapes, the brush moves like a dragon", and "The brush of Luang Pei, the stone drum, is a portrait of an orchid". This style of painting with calligraphy has had a profound influence on the creation of modern Chinese painting.　　In addition, the painting's ink is thick and steady, and the composition is unconventional and skillful in setting up the situation. The vivid brushwork and ink give the vibrancy of the wisteria vine, and the painting fully demonstrates the poem inscribed on this painting: "The luxuriant Ying drapes the purple jade, and the stripes are tied to the good spring light. The flowers grow well over the years and fill the painting hall." The poetic mood of the poem.
